> Hello,

> I'm trying to estimate ∫f(lw)*f(x,y | exp(lw))dw, where f(lw) is an already-estimated mixture model (using mclust).  However, I keep getting "NA/NaN function evaluation" from nlminb and I'm not quite sure exactly why.
>
> R code:
>
> library(TMB)
> library(mclust)
> dw <- densityMclust(log(w_o))
>
>
> parameters <- list(
> lw = rep(0, length(y)),
> gamma_wy = -0.7,
> gamma_wxy = -0.7,
> gamma_wx = -0.7,
> lsigma_y = -0.7,
> lsigma_x = -0.7,
> mu_y = 0,
> mu_x = 0,
> b = 0
> )
>
> data <- list(
> x = x,
> y = y,
> dw_mean = dw$parameters$mean,
> dw_prop = dw$parameters$pro,
> dw_sigma = sqrt(dw$parameters$variance$sigmasq)
> )
>
> compile("file.cpp")
> dyn.load(dynlib("file"))
> obj <- MakeADFun(
> data=data, parameters=parameters,
> DLL="file",
> random=c("lw")
> )
>
> opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
>
> Then, in C++/TMB:
>
> #include <TMB.hpp>
>
> template<class Type>
> vector<Type> dw(vector<Type> lw, vector<Type> means, vector<Type> prop, vector<Type> sigma)
> {
> vector<Type> res(lw.size());
>
> for (int i = 0; i < lw.size(); i++)
> {
> res(i) = 0;
> for (int j = 0; j < means.size(); j++)
> {
> res(i) += prop(j)*dnorm(lw(i), means(j), sigma(j), false);
> }
> }
>
> return log(res);
> }
>
> template<class Type>
> Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
> {
> DATA_VECTOR(x);
> DATA_VECTOR(y);
> DATA_VECTOR(dw_mean);
> DATA_VECTOR(dw_prop);
> DATA_VECTOR(dw_sigma);
> PARAMETER_VECTOR(lw);
> PARAMETER(gamma_wy);
> PARAMETER(gamma_wxy);
> PARAMETER(gamma_wx);
> PARAMETER(lsigma_y);
> PARAMETER(lsigma_x);
> PARAMETER(mu_y);
> PARAMETER(mu_x);
> PARAMETER(b);
> vector<Type> w = exp(lw);
>
> Type nll = -dw(lw, dw_mean, dw_prop, dw_sigma).sum();
>
> nll -= dnorm(y,
>               mu_y + b*x + gamma_wy*w + gamma_wxy*w*x,
>               exp(lsigma_y), true).sum();
> nll -= dnorm(x,
>               mu_x + gamma_wx*w,
>               exp(lsigma_x), true).sum();
> return nll;
> }
>
>
> The original w_o are distributed as Beta(2,5), and the prop values sum to 1.  The issue doesn't seem to be in dw or exp(lw), as removing them doesn't stop the problem.  It actually seems to be in the dnorm call for x, as the issue does go away when it's removed, but I can't figure out why.  Dropping lsigma_x (and relevant parameter stuff) and just using 1 for the variance gives the same issue, but so does dropping mu_x + gamma_wx*w (and relevant parameter stuff) and replacing it with 0.  Even dropping both yields the same, so it's got to be x itself.  x doesn't have any NA values though (values: https://pastebin.com/vv50R82R), and R's dnorm works fine on it.  It would be great if someone could help me out here.
>
> Thank you,
> Josh.
>

Hi, here's the full R code with the data generation:

set.seed(123)
library(TMB)
library(mclust)

w <- 1/rbeta(10000, 2, 5)
x <- rnorm(10000)
y <- 5 + 0.3*x - 0.5*x*w + rnorm(10000)

pop_df <- data.frame(x=x, y=y, w_o=w)
df <- pop_df[sample(10000, 500, prob = w),]

dw <- densityMclust(log(df$w_o))

parameters <- list(
lw = rep(0, nrow(df)),

gamma_wy = -0.7,
gamma_wxy = -0.7,
gamma_wx = -0.7,
lsigma_y = -0.7,
lsigma_x = -0.7,
mu_y = 0,
mu_x = 0,
b = 0
)

data <- list(

x = df$x,
y = df$y,

dw_mean = dw$parameters$mean,
dw_prop = dw$parameters$pro,
dw_sigma = sqrt(dw$parameters$variance$sigmasq)
)

compile("file.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("file"))
obj <- MakeADFun(
data=data, parameters=parameters,
DLL="file",
random=c("lw")
)

system.time(opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr))

messages.body_plain:
The Laplace approximation that is used for intergration does not work well with a mixture prior on the latent variable (needs to be Gaussian).

If you want to do this in TMB you are probably better off using numerical quadrature:

http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/namespaceromberg.html#a980bb141c963b1cf20da450063c5c7d1

messages.subject: TMB::normalize question with reproducible example.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was hoping I could get a better understanding of the syntax for using TMB::normalize.  I have data simulated here where two random effects vectors are distributed from GMRF.

The first model does not use TMB::normalize(), and fits correctly.
The second one (multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized.cpp) tries to use flags and TMB::normalize(), and does not seem to converge correctly.
Does anyone have an idea?

Thanks,
Dan

library(Matrix)
library(TMB)

compile("multiple_gmrf_random_effects.cpp")
compile("multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("multiple_gmrf_random_effects"))
dyn.load(dynlib("multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized"))

n<-50000
k<-10
X<-cbind(rep(1, n), matrix(runif(n*k),ncol=k))
beta<-rnorm(k+1)
sd_a<-.3
sd_b<-.1

### GMRF #1 (sparse block diagonal covariance for groups )
Ga1<-matrix(.5, 4, 4)  ## covariance within a group
diag(Ga1)<-1
grp<-rep(1:(n/4), each=4)
Qa<-as(chol2inv(chol(.bdiag(rep(list(Ga1),times=n/4)))), "dgTMatrix")

ua<-as.vector(t(chol(chol2inv(chol(Qa))))%*%matrix(rnorm(n, 0, sd_a), ncol=1))

### GMRF #2 (sparse block diagonal covariance for groups )
Gb1<-matrix(.25, 8, 8)  ## covariance within a group
diag(Gb1)<-1
Qb<-as(chol2inv(chol(.bdiag(rep(list(Gb1),times=n/8)))), "dgTMatrix")

ub<-as.vector(t(chol(chol2inv(chol(Qb))))%*%matrix(rnorm(n, 0, sd_b), ncol=1))

sd(ua); sd(ub)

y<-as.vector(X%*%beta + ua + ub + rnorm(n))

dl<-list(y=y,
     X=X,
     Qa=Qa,
     Qb=Qb,
         flaga=1,
         flagb=1)

parameters <- list(
                   log_sdres = 0,
                   log_sd_a = 0,
                   log_sd_b = 0,
                   a            = rep(0.0, n),
                   b            = rep(0.0, n),
                   beta          = rep(0, ncol(X))
                  )

obj <- MakeADFun(dl, parameters, random=c("a", "b"), DLL="multiple_gmrf_random_effects")
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
### works

dl<-list(y=y,
     X=X,
     Qa=Qa,
     Qb=Qb,
         flaga=0,
         flagb=0)

obj2 <- MakeADFun(dl, parameters, random=c("a", "b"), DLL="multiple_gmrf_random_effects_unnormalized")
obj2<-TMB::normalize(obj2,flag=c("flaga", "flagb"))
opt2 <- nlminb(obj2$par, obj2$fn, obj2$gr)
### doesn't work

messages.body_plain:
>From ?normalize:

"In order for this to work, the model must include a flag that disables the data term so that the un-normalized random effect (negative log) density is returned from the model template."

Example:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_examples/spde_aniso_speedup.cpp

You only need one flag. Why do you have two?
The template should look something like the following (flag==0 disables the data term as required by the documentation):

  nll += GMRF(Qa, false)(a);
  nll += GMRF(Qb, false)(b);
  if(flag == 0) return nll; // Return without data term
  for( int j=0; j<X.rows(); j++){
    nll -= dnorm( y(j) , eta(j), exp(log_sdres), true );
  }
  return nll;

messages.subject: Contradictory messages
messages.body_plain:
Dear TMB developers.

I would like to report our findings, which might help to improve TMB.  While we have run an inference in TMB (i.e., the set of MakeADFun and nlmin) using simulated data, we found that, despite the

warning message, “Hessian of fixed effects was not positive definite”, other output elements misled us by showing successful convergence (e.g., $convergence of 0), the presence of the covariance matrix

of estimates (e.g., from sdreport(model)$cov, or sdreport(model)$cov.fixed), and the presence of the standard errors of estimates, etc.  I am saying the contradiction between the warning message vs. those

output elements that imply successful inferences.  Estimates of *the standard errors* of parameters (fixed effects) in this case were very unreasonable (yes, it makes sense thanks to the warning message),

when being compared with the (known) true values of parameters (fixed effects), from which data had been simulated.

Please see the example of our findings below.

(1)   Note the warning message below in red.

> sdreport(xxx$model);

sdreport(.) result

               Estimate      Std. Error

loga       0.5260281   0.4325290

logb       0.4163987 218.1806116

logsig_p  -2.1019463   0.3286204

logK      17.2359107 218.1826011

logq     -19.4894820   3.7650666

logr     -14.0591460 274.7474254

Warning:

          Hessian of fixed effects was not positive definite.

Maximum gradient component: 4.912905e-05

(2)   But the covariance matrix of estimates was generated

      > sdreport(xxx$model)$cov.fixed;

                   loga          logb    logsig_p          logK       logq          logr

       loga      0.18708133 -1.569927e-02 -0.13404870 -2.011561e-01  0.2060882 -5.704039e-02

       logb     -0.01569927  4.760278e+04  0.01386906 -4.759614e+04 -6.5953252 -7.548696e+04

       logsig_p -0.13404870  1.386906e-02  0.10799136  1.642217e-01 -0.1704407  4.821895e-02

       logK     -0.20115615 -4.759614e+04  0.16422169  4.760365e+04 -7.5518510  7.547677e+04

       logq      0.20608823 -6.595325e+00 -0.17044069 -7.551851e+00 14.1757265  1.014200e+01

       logr     -0.05704039 -7.548696e+04  0.04821895  7.547677e+04 10.1420020  7.548615e+04

Suggestion:   If you think our findings are valid, then it may be a good idea to follow the custom of ADMB.  For instance, if Hessian matrix is not positive definite, COR file is not generated under ADMB.

A user *immediately* gets a sense by finding the absence of COR file that the corresponding numerical optimization is not reliable .  On the other hand, a user would be tricked under TMB unless he/she

carefully searches the warning message.   Especially when a user runs an inference in TMB, using thousands of sets of simulated data, he/she would have to manually find the warning message per run; nobody

would want to do so thousand times.   If Hessian matrix is not positive definite, your setting the convergence flag to be 1 (Failure) not 0 (Success), or your replacing the covariance matrix of

estimates by NA under TMB would be consistent, more importantly helping a user to quickly discard such unreliable inferences.

Thank you very much for your great development of TMB, and also thank you in advance for your reading this email.

Saang-Yoon Hyun, and Kyuhan Kim

messages.subject: Re: Alternative parameterization for SPDE method
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
If you're looking at this paper https://www.stat.washington.edu/peter/591/Lindgren.pdf the marginal variance is described in equation 2 , and  rho can be inferred from equation 5 in terms of kappa.  you could code them to be output like this:

Type range = sqrt(8)/kappa;   //Distance at which correlation has dropped to 0.1
Type  marginal_variance = pow(exp(.5*log(Type(1.0)/(Type(4.0)*M_PI)) - ln_kappa - ln_tau),2);

Assuming alpha=2, and your spatial data is 2-d (d=2).

Thanks for your reply,

and apologies for the confusion which is probably due to my limited understanding.

I am aware that sdreport() gives me the standard errors, but I was interested in the full covariance matrix because I have some correlation structure modeled in the random effects, and so am thinking that the covariances may be non-negligible.

say
jp<-sdreport(obj,getJointPrecision=TRUE)$jointPrecision

and

solve(jp)

or

Matrix::chol2inv(Matrix::chol(jp))
  Cholmod error 'problem too large' at file ../Core/cholmod_dense.c, line 105

are too large of a problem, because for example "ub", and "uc" may be 100 times longer vectors than "ua", and "ua" is my primary interest.

Solving the submatrix of jp
corresponding to random effect vector "ua" is really not correct, and underestimates the standard errors by a factor.

summary(sqrt(diag(solve(jp[rownames(jp)=="ua",rownames(jp)=="ua"]))) / mysdsummary[param=="ua",`Std. Error`])
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.
 0.3049  0.6619  0.7745  0.7424  0.8370  0.9319

 cor(sqrt(diag(solve(jp[rownames(jp)=="ua",rownames(jp)=="ua"]))),mysdsummary[param=="ua",`Std. Error`])
[1] 0.9590948

So, I'm wondering what the best approximation / easiest workaround might be.  It seems that internally the calculation has already been made by sdreport(), otherwise I wouldn't have the standard errors.

Do you think the best workaround may involve using model$he(), and calling "ua" a fixed effect, ?

Or is there another way to output this report, without requiring a full covariance matrix for all random effects, i.e. "ub", "uc", ...?

Thanks very much,
Dan

> turn "ua" into a fixed effect.

> Hans
